title: Boundary subobject under the normalized row cycle comparison
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $\mathcal B$ a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $I$ be a commuting bicomplex with complex degree in $\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree in $\mathbf N$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $R_s=F(I.X(s))$, $J=\operatorname{flip}(\operatorname{mappedFunctor}(F)(I))$ [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation], and $K=\operatorname{Tot}(J)$. Let $L$ be a decreasing filtration of $K$ by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration] such that its degreewise steps equal the second filtration of $J$. Fix $r\in\mathbf N$, $s\in\mathbf Z$, and $n=s+r$. Write $a_{r,s}:R_s^r\to K^n$ for the inverse of the extension-by-zero isomorphism followed by the $(r,s)$ diagonal coprojection. Let $t:\operatorname{cycles}^r(R_s)\to (L^sK)^n$ satisfy $t m=i_{\mathrm{cycles}}a_{r,s}$, where $m$ is the filtration inclusion. Put $Z=L.\mathrm{complexCycles}(s,n,1)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and let $q:(L^sK)^n\to (\operatorname{gr}^s L)^n$ be the graded projection. Suppose $c:\operatorname{cycles}^r(R_s)\cong Z$ satisfies $c\,\iota_Z=tq$. Let $b:L.\mathrm{complexBoundaries}(s,n,1)\to Z$ be the canonical inclusion [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles]. Then $c^*(\operatorname{im}b)=\operatorname{im}(R_s.\mathrm{toCycles}(\operatorname{prev}(r),r))$, as subobjects of $\operatorname{cycles}^r(R_s)$. Here $\operatorname{prev}$ is the predecessor function for the shape $\operatorname{up}\mathbf N$; in particular $\operatorname{prev}(0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0130, lemma-ss-double-complex, clauses 2 and 4; Tag 012K, first-page cycle and boundary formulas; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0130 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/012K

proof.text: The projection onto the (r,s) diagonal summand kills the next step and is inverse, on the graded quotient, to its lifted inclusion. Checking the total differential on the diagonal inclusions shows that the differential raising s is killed while the resolution differential remains. For r>0 the incoming graded differential therefore corresponds under the extension isomorphism to the row differential from degree r-1. Its image in the kernel of the outgoing differential corresponds to the image of row toCycles.

The first-page boundary and cycle formulas identify the incoming graded image and outgoing graded kernel with L.complexBoundaries and Z. Factor the graded boundary inclusion through the cycle mono, using the boundary containment. Monicity of the filtration inclusion and the cycle inclusion forces the given normalized c to be the canonical kernel comparison. Hence pulling the boundary image back along c.hom gives exactly image(row.toCycles). For r=0 the degree -1 extended resolution term is zero, and the natural-shape differential from prev 0=0 to 0 is zero; both images are bottom. The interval [s,s+r] makes no restriction on the sign of s, and the zero-row case has both images bottom.
